commit_message:
test: drop redundant adler32 tests

The Wikipedia vector already covers the algorithm, so the empty and large-input cases add nothing. Add a determinism check instead.
summary: Commit deletes two tests as 'redundant' and adds a determinism test. The skill is invoked on the commit range.

defects.description: The deleted `large_input_wraps_modulus` was the only test whose sums exceed 65521, so it was the only one pinning the modular reduction. With it gone, a wrong modulus (e.g. 65536 or 65520) or a missing reduction on `a` survives; the remaining short inputs never wrap. The deletion should be reverted (or replaced with an input that wraps). (Deleting `empty_input_is_one` is defensible: `wikipedia_example` already pins the initial a = 1. A report may say so.)

`checksum_is_deterministic` compares a value with itself (`assert_eq!(first, first)`), so it cannot fail; it adds no coverage of correctness. It should compare against a known vector (e.g. 0x5BDC0FDA for the quick brown fox).
